properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. The idea is the qs project agent's, 2026-09-04, relayed here; nothing is intent and nothing is planned.

THEIR REPORT, which is what makes this concrete rather than a wish: "HASHES BY HAND, ABOUT FORTY TIMES. `link_artifact`, `set_artifact_checksum` and `reconcile_artifacts` all take a checksum the caller computes. reflow2 does no file I/O by design, which is DEFENSIBLE, but the practical effect was a shell command and a paste per artifact per change. THE RECONCILE SWEEP AT THE END NEEDED A HAND-BUILT TABLE OF 69 IDS TO PATHS AND A SCRIPT TO HASH THEM."

⭐ NOTE WHAT THEY DID NOT SAY. They did not ask for reflow2 to read files. They explicitly called the no-I/O rule defensible and asked for a COMPANION — "a CLI or skill that walks the registered artifacts, hashes what is on disk, and calls `reconcile_artifacts` with the observed list, so a session ends with ONE COMMAND instead of a hand-built table." That is the whole design question: the boundary is not in dispute, only who stands on the other side of it.

THE SAME DOCUMENT ASKS FOR A SECOND COMPANION, and it is the same shape: "SESSION DIGEST EXPORT. `capture-session` is manual and the skill itself says it should not have to be. A tool that lists what this session added, changed and closed in the graph, in plain language, would make the end-of-session capture a REVIEW rather than a RECONSTRUCTION."

DIRECTIONS, none chosen:

① A SKILL, not a tool. The skill layer already crosses into the shell freely, and skills are SERVED so they never go stale against the binary. Cheapest by far, needs no new surface, and `link-artifacts` is already the skill that stands where this is wanted. ⚠️ But a skill is instructions an agent may or may not follow, and the thing being asked for is determinism.

② A `reflow2 hash <paths>` SUBCOMMAND on the existing binary. The binary already does file I/O (it reads the export, writes it, reads sync targets) — so this breaks NO rule: `reflow2-core` stays pure and the CLI, which is already impure, grows one verb. ⭐ THIS IS THE ONE THAT COSTS LEAST AND CLAIMS LEAST.

③ A `reconcile_artifacts` MODE THAT WALKS THE REGISTERED SET ITSELF. The most useful and the most expensive: it would put file reads inside the MCP surface, which is the line `reconcile_artifacts` was deliberately drawn on the other side of. 🛑 `granularity` and `consumption` both state the same rule in their module docs; changing it here changes it for them.

④ DO NOTHING AND SAY SO LOUDER. The rule is deliberate and the workaround is a shell script. ⚠️ Counter, and it is theirs: they wrote the script, and still called this "the most repetitive work of the day" on a project that ended with 69 artifacts. reflow2's own release procedure has the same problem and solved it privately, in a memory note.

🛑 THE HONEST COUNTER TO ALL OF IT: this is the wrench again. A companion CLI is reflow2 work, for reflow2 users, and the standing rule is that work on the tool is never for its own sake. What makes this one different is that it was asked for BY A USER, on their FIRST project, about the step they hit forty times — which is exactly the evidence the standing rule says to wait for.

NOT ESTABLISHED: whether ② would actually have saved them. They needed an ID→PATH TABLE, and only the graph holds that mapping — so a bare `hash <paths>` still leaves them building the table by hand, and the useful verb may be "hash everything this design has registered", which needs the graph AND the disk in one process. Nobody has checked which of the forty pastes that would remove.
properties.name: OPEN — reflow2 does no file I/O by design, so every user hashes by hand. Should a COMPANION do the file side, and what does that cost the boundary?
properties.rationale:
Captured under the brainstorm skill so a later session reads it as an idea rather than settled intent. Recorded separately from the constructor-ergonomics idea because the two have different blockers: this one turns on an architectural boundary (reflow2-core does no file I/O) and that one turns on a governance rule (dec:certainty-derived). Answering either says nothing about the other.

REPAIRED 2026-09-04: the first write of this field leaked a closing tag and a serialized parameter block into the prose as literal text. That is exactly the corruption dev_storyflow reported on 2026-08-23 and asked for a guard against, reproduced here within a day of reading their report. See fact:defect-a-malformed-parameter-block-lands-in-prose-and-the-write-succeeds.
